name: coredata<-
title: Replacing the Core Data of Objects

origin.description: coredata<- writes value into the existing shape. The lengths must match. A matrix is filled down columns and keeps the series dimensions.

arguments.name: x
arguments.text: An object. A zoo series stores observations separately from its index.

arguments.name: value
arguments.text: A vector or matrix with the same number of observations.

origin.details: coredata<- writes value into the existing shape. The lengths must match. A matrix is filled down columns and keeps the series dimensions.
origin.value: The series with new observations. The index is unchanged.
origin.example:
x <- zoo(1:4, 10:13)
coredata(x) <- 5:8
cat(paste(coredata(x), collapse = " "), "\n", sep = "")

translation.value: The series with new observations. The index is unchanged.
translation.example:
import numpy as np
from zoo.series import Zoo
from zoo.coredata import coredata, coredata_set
x = coredata_set(Zoo(np.array([1, 2, 3, 4]), [10, 11, 12, 13]), [5, 6, 7, 8])
print(" ".join(str(int(v)) for v in coredata(x)))
